event: Heart rate, respiratory rate, and temperature are within normal limits; no acute distress observed.
Directed to triage for further evaluation of ear pain.
Mild erythema and moderate tenderness were newly noted around the right outer ear; the patient was afebrile with no systemic signs of illness.
A clinician review with otoscopic examination was planned to confirm the diagnosis and determine treatment.
Patient is irritable, frequently crying, and refusing normal feeds, with pulling at the right ear.

Examination shows right auricular erythema and tenderness, with a bulging tympanic membrane and middle-ear effusion; no mastoiditis, cellulitis, systemic infection, facial weakness, or neck stiffness.
Diagnosed with acute otitis media with effusion.
Oral paracetamol 120 mg was administered in the ED for pain relief, with continuation every 4–6 hours as needed.
Referred to Paediatrics/ENT for planned inpatient admission and further management; accepted under the paediatric ward team.
Oral amoxicillin 125 mg three times daily for 5 days is prescribed.
Parents are advised to monitor for systemic illness or worsening symptoms and seek medical review if these occur.
Reassessment is advised in 48 hours if there is no improvement, or earlier if the condition deteriorates.
Paracetamol 120 mg oral suspension four times daily is planned for pain, with warm compresses advised for symptomatic relief.
Right acute otitis media with effusion is clinically improving, with reduced tympanic membrane erythema and effusion and significantly improved pain.
Patient is alert, interactive, comfortable, and has no signs of systemic infection or distress; observations are stable on room air.
Patient tolerated oral amoxicillin and analgesia overnight without adverse effects.
Discharge later today is planned with a 5-day course of oral amoxicillin and paracetamol as needed for pain.
ENT follow-up in 2 weeks is planned, with discharge medication dosing and completion of antibiotics to be explained to the parents.
